clue.text: Hero filmed tackling last of defenders, player collecting a knock

indicators.note: to tackle is to take hold of, so the hero's name grips the next letter

parts.note: the caped crusader of comics, much filmed, is Batman

indicators.note: asks for only the final letter of the word defenders

explanation.surface: A superhero in a film grappling with the back line of a defence, a player taking a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock is cricket slang for an innings, so the player collecting one is at the crease with a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player who scores runs is the one who has an innings, informally called a knock.

clue.text: Warmer? B*** hot!

parts.note: a censored swear word leaves only its initial on show
hot in the sense of lustful means randy

explanation.surface: Someone shivering asks for something to warm them, swearing about how hot it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisks pretend to bleep a rude word; all that survives is the letter at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass of spirit is traditionally taken to warm someone up from the inside.

clue.text: Work on film that's panned?

parts.note: hard work is toil
E.T. is Spielberg's film, a crossword standby for these two letters

explanation.surface: A movie being worked on that the critics then slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panned' looks like harsh reviewing, but the definition means fitted with a pan, the bowl of a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavatory has a pan as its bowl, so it is the thing that is panned, a punning description.

clue.text: Anyone can come to enter card game with inclination for fraud

indicators.note: the U slips inside the card game's name

parts.note: monte is a gambling card game, as in three-card monte
a U certificate film is open to anyone, so the phrase gives U
a bank is a slope, an inclination of the ground

explanation.surface: A card game anyone can join, set up with a leaning towards cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all, hence anyone can come.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindling quack who sold bogus remedies from a platform became the type of any charlatan or cheat.

clue.text: Depth from which she leaves Irish playwright to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom upwards
the pronoun she departs from the playwright's name

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, Dublin-born author of The Rivals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A low point from which a woman walks out on an Irish dramatist who goes on to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking SHE from SHERIDAN leaves RIDAN, and 'to rise' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything, its depths, is by extension the astronomical point directly below the observer.

clue.text: Girl inhaling smoke lying back, one capturing the image?

indicators.note: lying back means the assembled letters are read in reverse
the girl breathes in, so her name holds the smoke

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl
a cig is a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: A girl reclining with a cigarette, while someone photographs her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' is the old word maid, and 'lying back' turns the whole assembly round, which the surface hides as a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact digital camera records pictures, so it is something that captures the image.

clue.text: Animal spotted barking at animal with spotted tail

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
barking means mad, so the letters of at animal go crazy

explanation.surface: A dog seen yapping at another creature with a dappled tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The D from the tail of spotted goes first, then 'barking' rearranges AT ANIMAL into ALMATIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is famous for its white coat covered in black spots.

clue.text: See 28
Red key

definitions.meaning: a deep scarlet colour, as worn by princes of the Church
chief, fundamental, as in a key point

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a vivid scarlet hue and something of chief importance, as in principal virtues.

clue.text: Signature believed to be 11

parts.note: someone who cannot write signs with a mark
to have felt something is to have believed it

explanation.surface: A signature thought to belong to an anonymous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer at 11, the secret Watergate informant.
explanation.definitionFit: The FBI deputy director revealed in 2005 as the Watergate source codenamed Deep Throat.

clue.text: Parting message, wind up in my guts?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the guts are the insides, so only the inner letters of the setter's name remain

parts.note: the setter, Paul, speaks of himself, so my points to his name
to wind up is to end, to die

explanation.surface: A goodbye blurted as indigestion rumbles in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter here is Paul; his guts are AU, and DIE sits in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell, borrowed into English for a final goodbye.

clue.text: One saving another animal, implanting organ

indicators.note: the deer has the organ placed within it

parts.note: a deer, following the dog of the neighbouring clue
the liver is a body organ

explanation.surface: A rescuer of a second creature performs an organ transplant on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer or saviour delivers people from danger, setting them free.

clue.text: River grass encircling path, not a river grass

indicators.note: the river and grass together wrap round the following letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
oat is a cereal grass

indicators.note: not means the letter a is struck out of the word path

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A list of waterside plants around a footpath, read like a botanist's notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' strips A from PATH to give PTH; the final 'grass' is the definition, meaning an informer, not a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an informer is a grass, and this was the codename of the leaker behind the Watergate stories.

clue.text: A bit of jazz as a duty? No thanks!

indicators.note: no thanks says the thank-you is refused, so it comes off

parts.note: a tariff is a duty charged on imports
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone declining jazz as a chore, politely saying no thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A short repeated phrase played in jazz or rock is a recognised musical figure.

clue.text: Chap distanced from German conceit, terribly selfish

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters being badly mixed
the man is taken away from the word German

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man keeps his distance from a vain German, who is dreadfully self-absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: GERMAN without MAN leaves GER; 'terribly' shuffles GER and CONCEIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-centred thinks only of themselves, which is the essence of selfishness.

clue.text: One going down the lane in front, swimmer having a good time

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
the ling is a fish of the cod family
to have a ball is to have a great time

explanation.surface: A swimmer leading the field in their lane, having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The lane is a ten-pin bowling alley, not a swimming lane.
explanation.definitionFit: In ten-pin bowling the heavy sphere rolls down the polished lane towards the pins.

clue.text: Story exposed by 11, Washington target surprisingly ending in remorse?

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

indicators.note: surprisingly tells us the word target turns up in an unexpected order
takes only the final letter of remorse

explanation.surface: A scandal leaked by a mole, aiming at Washington and ending in regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges TARGET into TERGAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The scandal that brought down President Nixon was broken with help from the informant at 11.

clue.text: A number brought up on credit reduced by 25% — I'm not sure

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a number is a song in a show

indicators.note: a quarter of the four-letter word, its final letter, is cut

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A tune revived and bought on credit at a quarter off, the buyer unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK loses one of its four letters, its last, to give TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known declares themselves unsure.

clue.text: Tiny gap amongst cracks filled with last of mortar

indicators.note: the broken letters have another put into them
the word amongst cracks, breaking into a new order
only the final letter of mortar

explanation.surface: A small gap between cracked bricks, plugged with the end of the mortar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' rearranges AMONGST into ANGSTOM, with the R going in.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length of one ten-billionth of a metre, so any gap it measures is minute.

clue.text: Drink from greasiest lips?

parts.note: the lips of a word are its edges, and the edges of greasiest are G and T

explanation.surface: A cocktail sipped from very oily lips.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of greasiest are G and T, the everyday shorthand for this drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit topped up with a quinine mixer is a classic long drink.

clue.text: Something usually round around a square

indicators.note: the round thing goes around the letter

parts.note: a pizza is normally circular

explanation.surface: A riddle about a round object surrounding a square shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian town square or open public space.

clue.text: Budgie perhaps in existence, though not a bird

parts.note: a budgerigar is an example of a pet

indicators.note: says the letter a is left out of the word for existing

parts.note: something real actually exists
taken as written

explanation.surface: A budgie said to exist yet not to be a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL without A leaves REL.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the open ocean, named for St Peter walking on water.

clue.text: Cook won't open oven

indicators.note: the word for cook lacks its opening letter

parts.note: to roast is to cook

explanation.surface: A cook complaining that the oven door is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops, found especially in Kent, is a kind of oven.

clue.text: Giant waves in the sea for boat

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: the briny is the sea, and brine is salt water

indicators.note: waves suggests the letters of giant being tossed about

explanation.surface: Huge waves out at sea, for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' rearranges GIANT into GANTI; 'the sea' is the briny, salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel, square-rigged on the foremast.

clue.text: Flash Gordon loathes emperors, adversarial Ming for starters

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Flash Gordon hates emperors, particularly his enemy Ming the Merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' seems part of the hero's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light.

clue.text: Queen of Carthage was idle?

parts.note: was idle is did nothing, with did standing for the doing
idle means doing nothing, and nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question whether the ancient queen was lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'was idle' as 'did nothing': DID and O for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary founder and ruler of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil.

clue.text: Kill insect eating gnat after wings torn off

indicators.note: the insect swallows the next letters

parts.note: a termite is an insect

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, so only the middle of gnat remains

explanation.surface: An insect devours a gnat once its wings are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: GNAT minus its outer letters is NA.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to an end, and so in some uses to kill or exterminate.

clue.text: Laugh about rounding a couple of bends — one's sharp

indicators.note: the turned laugh goes round the next letters
about turns the word for laugh round

parts.note: to roar is to laugh loudly
the letter Z has two bends in its shape

explanation.surface: Laughter on a road with two hairpin bends, while someone sharp-witted drives.
explanation.walkthrough: ROAR reversed is RAOR, which wraps A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade for shaving is a keen-edged tool.

clue.text: Something to go on for naval officer — or not

indicators.note: not means the word or is left out

parts.note: a commodore is a naval rank above captain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval officer, or perhaps not, getting something to continue with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to go on' sounds like a lead, but it is a seat with a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair or cabinet housing a chamber pot is somewhere one goes, a polite euphemism.

clue.text: Leading Tory: "I have come last in poll, schooling ultimately a fiasco"

indicators.note: a fiasco is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
last in poll asks for the letter standing at the very end of that word, the final vote counted
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of schooling

explanation.surface: A senior Conservative bottom of the polls, his schools policy a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is I HAVE COME plus L and G, scrambled by 'a fiasco'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent Conservative cabinet minister of the 2010s, then Education Secretary.
